items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had worked with Hershel with some of my classical music. He had recorded a piece with the Western Arts Trio, a piece of mine called Contrasts.

ctx.x: . . . Keith Cronin on drums. And that really was a working group. I considered it a bebop group, but a bebop group with extended roots. And the very first album we did, which was simply called David Baker and the 21st Century Bebop Band . . . we took some standards. I did Hot House, but did it in a really different kind of way. I did a contrafact on Back Home in Indiana which I called Bebop Revisited, a piece called This One’s for Trane, and one other piece [An Evening Thought]. I can’t remember what it was. But…
